title: High-Volume Logging System
question: Design logging infrastructure for high-volume application. Requirements: 1) Application generates 100K log entries per second, 2) Logs must be searchable for troubleshooting, 3) Keep logs for 30 days, 4) Minimal performance impact on application, 5) Real-time alerting on errors, 6) Support for multiple environments (dev, staging, prod), 7) Cost-effective storage. Discuss: using asynchronous logging with AsyncAppender or async loggers to prevent blocking main threads, implementing structured JSON logging for easier parsing and searching, using log sampling for DEBUG level (log 1% of debug logs), shipping logs to centralized system using Filebeat or Fluent Bit agents on each server, using Kafka as intermediate buffer to handle bursts and decouple producers from consumers, processing logs with Logstash to parse, enrich, and transform, storing in Elasticsearch with hot-warm-cold architecture (recent logs in hot nodes for fast search, older logs in warm nodes, archive to S3 for compliance), implementing Index Lifecycle Management (ILM) to automatically transition indices, using Kibana for searching and visualization, setting up alerts in Elastalert or Kibana Watcher for error patterns (e.g., error rate exceeds threshold), implementing rate limiting on alerts to prevent alert fatigue, using different Elasticsearch clusters or indices per environment, implementing log retention policies (delete after 30 days), using compression for storage efficiency, and monitoring the logging pipeline itself for health.

title: Microservices Observability Platform
question: Implement comprehensive observability for 50 microservices. Requirements: 1) Trace requests across all services, 2) Correlate logs from different services for a single request, 3) Monitor service health and performance, 4) Alert on anomalies, 5) Debug production issues quickly, 6) Minimal code changes to services, 7) Handle 10K requests per second. Discuss: implementing distributed tracing with Spring Cloud Sleuth to automatically add trace and span IDs to logs and propagate them across services, using Zipkin or Jaeger as trace collector and UI, configuring sampling strategy (e.g., sample 10% of requests to reduce overhead, always sample error requests), using MDC to add trace ID to all log entries, implementing structured logging with JSON format including trace ID, span ID, service name, timestamp, log level, message, using ELK stack for log aggregation and searching (Filebeat ships logs from each service, Logstash parses JSON and enriches with metadata, Elasticsearch stores and indexes, Kibana for searching by trace ID to see all logs for a request), using Spring Boot Actuator to expose health and metrics endpoints, collecting metrics with Micrometer and shipping to Prometheus, creating Grafana dashboards for service health (request rate, error rate, latency percentiles), implementing service-level indicators (SLIs) and service-level objectives (SLOs), setting up alerts in Prometheus Alertmanager for SLO violations, implementing circuit breaker pattern with Resilience4j and monitoring circuit breaker states, using correlation ID propagation through HTTP headers (X-Correlation-ID), implementing centralized exception handling to log errors with full context, and using OpenTelemetry for future-proof observability instrumentation.

title: Production Issue Debugging Strategy
question: Production application experiencing intermittent errors affecting 1% of requests. Requirements: 1) Cannot reproduce in staging, 2) Errors are random and hard to trace, 3) Cannot enable DEBUG logs globally (performance impact), 4) Need to identify root cause, 5) Minimal customer impact, 6) Quick resolution. Discuss: implementing dynamic log level adjustment using Logback JMX or Spring Boot Actuator endpoints to enable DEBUG logs for specific packages or classes without restart, using MDC to add request ID to all logs for a single request, implementing request sampling (enable DEBUG logs for 1% of requests or specific user IDs), using conditional logging with markers to enable DEBUG logs only for requests matching criteria (e.g., specific customer ID, request path), implementing distributed tracing to identify which service is causing issues, using APM tools like Elastic APM or New Relic to identify slow transactions and errors, analyzing error patterns in Kibana to find commonalities (time of day, specific endpoints, user segments), implementing feature flags to disable problematic features for subset of users, using database query logging to identify slow or failing queries, implementing request/response logging for specific endpoints with sensitive data masking, using memory dumps and thread dumps to analyze application state, implementing health check endpoints to verify dependencies, using canary deployment to test fixes on small subset of traffic, implementing rollback strategy to quickly revert if fix doesn't work, and setting up comprehensive monitoring to detect when issue is resolved.

title: Compliance and Audit Logging System
question: Implement audit logging for financial application with compliance requirements. Requirements: 1) Log all user actions (login, transactions, data access), 2) Logs must be immutable and tamper-proof, 3) Keep audit logs for 7 years, 4) Support forensic analysis, 5) GDPR compliance (handle PII appropriately), 6) Generate audit reports, 7) Detect suspicious activities. Discuss: implementing separate audit logging system independent from application logs, using structured audit events with schema (timestamp, user ID, action type, resource, old value, new value, IP address, result), storing audit logs in write-once-read-many (WORM) storage or using blockchain for immutability, using database audit triggers for automatic logging of data changes, implementing separate audit log appender that writes to secure location, using message queue (Kafka) for audit events to ensure no loss and enable multiple consumers, implementing PII masking or tokenization in logs (e.g., show last 4 digits of SSN, hash email addresses), using role-based access control for audit log access, implementing log signing or hashing to detect tampering, storing logs in compliance-approved storage (AWS S3 with object lock, Azure immutable storage), implementing automatic archival to cold storage (Glacier) after certain period to reduce costs, using separate Elasticsearch cluster for audit logs with longer retention, implementing audit log search interface for compliance officers with fine-grained access control, generating compliance reports (user activity reports, access reports, change reports), implementing real-time anomaly detection on audit events (unusual access patterns, after-hours access, bulk data downloads), setting up alerts for suspicious activities, implementing audit log backup and disaster recovery, ensuring log timestamps are synchronized using NTP, and documenting audit logging procedures for compliance audits.
